title: iTutorGroup to Pay $365000 to Settle EEOC Discriminatory Hiring Suit
supports_claim: EEOC reported a $365000 settlement and that configured software automatically rejected more than 200 qualified older applicants.
limitations: Settlement announcement describes allegations and relief; it does not publish a technical model audit.

title: Amazon scraps secret AI recruiting tool that showed bias against women
supports_claim: Reuters reported that Amazon built an experimental resume-ranking model from 2014 and scrapped it in 2018 after it penalized resumes containing women-focused language.
limitations: Reporting relies on anonymous former employees and does not quantify deployed decisions or applicant counts.

title: Workday faces U.S. lawsuit claiming AI screening tool discriminates
supports_claim: Reuters reported that a job applicant sued Workday and alleged its AI screening tools discriminated against Black older and disabled applicants.
limitations: The suit is an allegation in litigation; no court ruling on the merits is cited.

title: Select Issues: Assessing Adverse Impact in Software Algorithms and Artificial Intelligence Used in Employment Selection Procedures
supports_claim: EEOC technical guidance explains how Title VII adverse-impact principles apply to AI and algorithmic employment selection tools.
limitations: Guidance is interpretive and not binding law; outcomes depend on the specific fact pattern.

title: Regulatory framework on artificial intelligence
supports_claim: The Commission identifies employment and workers-management AI as a high-risk area and publishes the staged AI Act application timeline.
limitations: Implementation dates and guidance can change and must be re-checked before deployment.

title: Law 134/2025/QH15 on Artificial Intelligence
supports_claim: Vietnam AI Law took effect on 2026-03-01 and establishes the governing legal scope for AI systems.
limitations: Exact obligations depend on role use case and implementing instruments that must be read together.

title: Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg high-risk AI list
supports_claim: The decision publishes Vietnam's list of high-risk AI systems and took effect on 2026-08-15.
limitations: A use case must be matched to the full official list; title metadata alone is insufficient for classification.
